one_liner: API-first uptime monitoring and status pages for indie devs and small teams — Terraform provider from day one.
description: pingdeck monitors HTTP endpoints, cron jobs, and TCP ports with 30-second intervals, then feeds alerts to Slack, email, or webhooks and renders clean public status pages. Everything is manageable through a full REST API and an official Terraform provider, so monitors live in code next to the infrastructure they watch.
target_user: Indie developers and small platform teams running production services

icp.who: Developers and 1-5 person platform teams operating 10-500 endpoints
icp.pain: UptimeRobot-class tools are click-ops with bolted-on APIs, while Datadog-class synthetic monitoring is priced for enterprises
icp.buying_trigger: An outage nobody noticed for an hour, or an infra-as-code migration that makes click-configured monitors feel like debt

differentiators: Full REST API and official Terraform provider shipped from day one — monitors as code, not click-ops
30-second check intervals on the free tier, where most competitors gate fast checks behind paid plans
Status pages, cron monitoring, and alerting included in one flat price
proof_points: Official Terraform provider published in the Terraform Registry
30-second intervals free, verified on the public pricing page
pricing_current: freemium (free for 10 monitors at 30s intervals, $10/month team plan)

voice.sample_phrase: Monitors as code. Alerts before your customers notice.

signals: Terraform provider in the public registry
Public status page with historical uptime

gaps: Only three alert integrations beyond webhooks

confidence.notes: API-first claims verifiable via docs and registry. Endpoint counts self-reported.
